rules_text:
Rules summary Token effects BIRTH (X3) (blue token with dino hatching from egg) Place a Diplo from your pool on the empty case of your choice. This token scores 1 point at the end of the game. RECON (X2) (blue token with dino walking) Secretly look at ALL the Grass tokens on a Pasture board of your choice, without moving them. This token scores 1 point at the end of the game. AIR TRAVEL (X4) (blue token with flying purple dino) Move any Diplo in the playing area to any empty space of your choice. This token scores 1 point at the end of the game. AIR RAID (X3) (orange token with flying purple dino) Move a T.Rex already in the playing area to any empty space of your choice. This token scores 1 point at the end of the game. VOLCANIC ERUPTION (X2) (orange token with volcano) Remove two Grass tokens from the playing area, without looking at them (put them back in the box). This token scores 1 point at the end of the game. SURPRISE (X2) (white token with red T rex) Replace your Diplo with a T.Rex from the edge of the playing area. Put your Diplo back in your pool. This token scores 3 points at the end of the game. YUMMY (X12) (yellow token with plant) The grass is tasty, but you benefit from no immediate effect. This token scores 2 points at the end of the game. End of game The game ends immediately when one of the three following conditions is fulfilled: One of the players has no Diplo left in the playing area; In this case, the player loses the game, and the amount of grass eaten by each player’s Diplos is not taken into account. Either there is no more Grass tokens in the playing area; During two turns in a row, NO player has taken a Grass token or scared away one of his opponent’s Diplos out of the playing area. In these last two cases, each player reveals all the Grass tokens his team of Diplos has eaten during the game. The player with the highest score wins the game! In case of a tie, the player with the least Grass tokens is the winner. If there is still a tie, the players share the victory!

[Rating: 3/10] I know it a kid's game, but it's actually kind of complex with needing to learn what all the different tiles do (the pictures are clear once you learn). The effects are randomly triggered when you land on and reveal a tile, so you can't plan for them. And it's so tedious if you get a Recon tile early on and get to secretly look at every tile (not sure if there's any real point remembering what is where).  Hey, That's My Fish feels similar but a much cleaner design, where all the tiles are face-up, no special effects, and it's all about most efficiently gathering up the points while avoiding ge

[Rating: 3.5/10] The dinosaurs and square grid board gave me some hope that Jurassic Snack was Cathala discovering that a streamlined reskin of one of his older designs could act as some sort of spiritual Raptor Junior. We are, unfortunately, in the design philosophy of making positional abstracts more palatable to kids by adding thick layers of randomness that trivialise almost any form of relevant decision-making. Very short, very swingy, and only somewhat held by plastic cartoon dinosaurs you can find in a toy shop for cheaper.

[Rating: 4/10] One of our first games, but it got pretty boring over time. The game is very nicely designed and fun at first, but it eventually becomes very repetitive, and even my son isn’t interested in it anymore; only my daughter asks to play it occasionally. The winner is whoever randomly collects points.

[Rating: 5/10] Cute push your luck game. Not a whole lot of strategy going on here, but it is quick and you get to play with dino figures! Geared towards kids and I think kids would enjoy it. I would try it again, I mean I won after all!

[Rating: 5/10] Tout comme la première version du jeu (Guerre et bêêêh), ce jeu à deux est très simple, très hasardeux (c'est un peu trop simple et un peu trop hasardeux pour moi). Ce n’est à mon avis pas la meilleure réussite de l’auteur, mais c'est sans doute le plus accessible. L’édition est très soignée, avec de magnifiques dinosaures.

[Rating: 5/10] I get that it is a children game, but there is nothing interesting game-wise whatsoever. Most of the game is just chance.  The components are adorable.
